key_insight: PoreML provides an end-to-end, physics-grounded machine-learning workflow for predicting multiphase flow in porous media by combining reproducible simulation, a large curated dataset, and standardized model evaluation.
engineering_relevance: The framework can accelerate design and assessment of porous-material systems relevant to CO2 storage, fuel cells, and flip-chip packaging by enabling faster surrogate models for complex fluid-interface dynamics.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale data generation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 stored time steps across four scenarios
Unified training/evaluation protocol for one-step prediction and autoregressive rollout tests
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 3.3 TB dataset spanning synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries, plus domain-specific evaluation of five models including transfer to larger domains and real-structure generalization.
watch_item: Model performance may still depend on how well training data cover wettability, viscosity-ratio, and geometry variability, so transfer to unseen porous structures could remain challenging.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
